title: the row's record page is the next page, and it reaches the step
line: once a FamilySearch results page saved for a fetch step has a row proposed as the step's person, the fetch list prints that row's own record page in the search link's place, under the record-page name with the row's ark filled, open until a page carrying the ark is archived; the record page saved and collected reaches the step through the listing that pointed at it, is archived under the step's citation, and closes the step: the row reads held and the list is empty for it

steps.say: a 1950 citation on the person, planted: the file cites none on him, so the step stands with its record id on the owner's word, the name the citation sits on as the search was run

step.rationale: harness: a 1950 citation on the owner's word; fetch the record at United States, Census, 1950

expect.why: before the search is saved, the step's own page is open for him

steps.say: the search saved: the first row is his card, and the row's own record page takes the search link's place on the list

expect.why: the step's own page is gone from the list: a row of the search points on
the row's own record page, under the record-page name with the ark filled and the row's year, open for his step

steps.say: the record page saved in the browser into the download folder under the name the list printed
collect brings it in by its own identity: it reaches the step through the listing that pointed at it, archived under the step's citation, and the step is done

expect.why: the page names no sheet the citations name and its principal is Fred, not Frederick, so neither the census-page route nor the collection fallback reaches him: the listing's row does
archived under the step's citation, as any record page a step cites
a record page holds the citation: the step is done
two runs: the listing, then the record it pointed at
the son alone is proposed on the record page; the household waits on him
the row reads held on the record page
the list is empty for it

steps.say: his plan run again keeps the step done: the archive holds its citation
